LFS 100.title: Introduction to Land, Food and Community
LFS 100.description: Orientation to the programs, learning environment and core values of the Faculty of Land and Food Systems; career programs; survey of professional opportunities and requirements.

LFS 101.title: Principles of Microeconomics with Applications to Land and Food Systems
LFS 101.description: Microeconomic principles focused on private and social decision making related to the use of land, especially in agriculture, forestry, and conservation. Restricted to Faculty of Land and Food Systems students in Land One Option.

LFS 110.title: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
LFS 110.description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both Indigenous and Western perspectives. Restricted to Faculty of Land and Food Systems students in the Land One option.

LFS 150.title: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Land and Food Systems
LFS 150.description: Communicating concepts of food systems and links to human and environmental health through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. Enrolment limited to LFS students with first year status.

LFS 250.title: Land, Food and Community I: Introduction to Food Systems and Sustainability
LFS 250.description: Managed systems and concepts of sustainability; economic, ecological and social components; managed landscapes, agri-food systems, and communities; urban and rural systems; the land, food, nutrition and human health continuum.

LFS 252.title: Land, Food, and Community: Quantitative Data Analysis
LFS 252.description: Introduction to tools needed for data analysis of the economic, ecological, health, and scientific components of land and food systems.
LFS 252.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100

LFS 301.title: Aquaculture Field Studies
LFS 301.description: An orientation to the aquaculture system in BC. Participating students are assessed a fee.

LFS 302.title: International Field Studies
LFS 302.description: Field studies carried out abroad under staff direction. Participating students are assessed a fee.

LFS 303.title: International Field Studies in Policy Analysis for Agriculture and Natural Resources
LFS 303.description: Field studies carried out abroad under the direction of the instructor. Students will be guided to apply selected tools for analysis of agricultural and natural resource policy in developing countries with input from local policymakers. Participating students are assessed a fee.
notes: Third-year standing and permission of instructor. 9 credits of upper level ECON, FRE or COMM courses are strongly recommended.

LFS 340.title: First Nations Health and the Traditional Role of Plants
LFS 340.description: This Interprofessional Health and Human Service (IHHS) course covers the First Nations medical systems and medicinal plants. Bridging the traditional with modern sciences.

LFS 350.title: Land, Food, and Community II: Principles and Practice of Community Food Security
LFS 350.description: Project-based application of the principles and processes of community food security. Emphasis on developing skills required to address economic, ecological, social, and technological components of managed landscapes, agri-food systems, and communities comprising the land, food, nutrition and health continuum.

LFS 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
LFS 398.description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail.

prerequisite.raw: Must attend all Co-op pre-employment workshops

LFS 398.prerequisiteText: Must attend all Co-op pre-employment workshops

LFS 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
LFS 399.description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail.

LFS 400.title: Audio Storytelling
LFS 400.description: Adopts a journalistic framework to communicate powerful stories and present academic content in new ways through the use of audio and podcasting technology.

LFS 402.title: Living Language: Science and Society
LFS 402.description: Multidisciplinary course in which students, individually and in groups, examine, integrate and apply subject-specific knowledge through the lens of language and the framework of the language sciences, with a focus on themes of real-world importance.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor

LFS 402.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor

LFS 450.title: Land, Food, and Community III: Leadership in Campus Food System Sustainability
LFS 450.description: Design, analysis, recommendation or implementation of solutions in response to a food sustainability issue faced by community partners. Emphasis is on professional communication, leadership development, project management and decision-making skills.

LFS 490.title: Topics in Land and Food Systems
LFS 490.description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues related to land and food systems.

LFS 496.title: Career Development Practicum
LFS 496.description: Practical application of degree program learning appropriate to students' career goals. Enrolment subject to competition and availability of practicum placements.

LFS 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
LFS 498.description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail.

LFS 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
LFS 499.description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail.

LFS 501.title: Approaches to the Integration of Knowledge
